1.1.0.lead: Sign in through several providers, as in every nex app: authentik, Microsoft Entra ID or any other that speaks OpenID Connect.

sections.title: Several sign-in providers
sections.body: Each provider gets a button on the sign-in page, in the order of your list. Per provider you choose whether new people get an account and whether it checks the second factor itself. Microsoft Entra ID works with several tenants too.

sections.title: authentik in one step
sections.body: With an API token nexpaper sets up provider and application in authentik itself and says for each step what worked and what did not. Who would rather not hand out a token downloads a blueprint instead.

sections.title: Linking in your account
sections.body: Every account links itself to the providers, with your password as confirmation, and undoes the link there. A mail address from the provider no longer links anything by itself; an invitation works through the provider too.

small: Your provider so far is the first entry of the list, every link stays, its redirect address too
An address from the provider counts for documents by mail only once you confirmed it
Behind a proxy nexpaper trusts, the scheme it reports counts too
The hints under “Require a second factor” now say that a provider which checks the second factor itself spares accounts with a password from it too

1.0.1.lead: A small version: nexpaper now says more clearly where it is best kept.

sections.title: Best kept at home
sections.body: Your papers are best kept in your own network, and from on the way you come in through a VPN. The texts about the API no longer promise apps that are still to come.

small: The README and the security notes say the same

1.0.0.lead: This is nexpaper 1.0, a filing cabinet for documents at home and in a small business: the simple Paperless-ngx for the home. This is what you find from the start.

sections.title: Everything comes into the inbox first
sections.body: From the phone, the mailbox, the intake folder, Paperless or the browser: new files wait in the inbox with the fields filled in. Filter by vault, search the text too, look at every page large, and file many at once.

sections.title: Vaults
sections.body: Everybody has a vault of their own, and there are shared ones like “Household”. Sharing is read, edit or manage, and single documents can go out as a link.

sections.title: Organise
sections.body: Senders, kinds and tags in one place, with how many documents each has: rename, merge or delete them. Typing a sender or a tag proposes the ones you already have.

sections.title: Text recognition and search
sections.body: Scans become searchable PDFs and the original stays as it came. The search understands parts of words and filters like “kind:”, “sender:” and “amount:>”.

sections.title: Photographing with edge detection
sections.body: The camera finds the sheet, takes the picture by itself and straightens it. Several pages become one document.

sections.title: Pages and versions
sections.body: Turn, delete and order pages, join documents or split them at blank separator sheets. Every change is saved as a version of the document, the original stays.

sections.title: Backup and checking the files
sections.body: The backup holds the database, the settings and the server secrets, not the documents and not the search index. Once a week nexpaper checks the checksums of all files and warns at the document when one is missing or has changed.

small: E-invoices (ZUGFeRD, Factur-X, XRechnung) are read from their data
Kinds of their own per vault, and rules that help with filing
An export for the tax adviser as a ZIP, as a link if you like
From the iPhone with a shortcut, from Android through Share
A second factor, passkeys and sign-in through your own provider
